q: What is `0 || 5000`? What is `0 ?? 5000`? Which one do you use for defaults?
a: 0 || 5000 is 5000 (|| replaces every falsy value). 0 ?? 5000 is 0 (?? only replaces null and undefined). Use ?? for defaults.

q: What is the difference between `break` and `continue` in a loop?
a: continue skips the rest of THIS round and goes to the next item. break stops the whole loop.

q: A switch case returns the value of the NEXT case. What is the bug?
a: A missing break (fall-through). Every case must end with break or return.

q: When does the `finally` block run?
a: Always: after try if there was no error, after catch if there was one. Use it for cleanup.

q: Error: "'error' is of type 'unknown'." inside catch. Why, and how do you fix it?
a: JavaScript can throw anything, so TypeScript types the caught error as unknown. Check it first: if (error instanceof Error) { error.message }.

q: Error: "Matcher error: received value must be a function" with toThrow. Fix?
a: You passed the RESULT of the call: expect(fn()). Pass a function instead: expect(() => fn()).toThrow().

q: Error: "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')". What happened?
a: You read .city on something that is undefined (for example user.address). Use optional chaining: user.address?.city.

q: Why is `for (let i = 0; i <= items.length; i++)` a bug?
a: Indexes go from 0 to length - 1. With <= the last round reads items[length], which is undefined. Use <.
